rubric_notes: Correct and bundle-supported hierarchy: a.22.1.1-4 plus a.22.1.0 with members; homology endpoint cited correctly; notes no fold-only relatives exist in 2.08. Clearly states superfamily supports probable common ancestry but does not transfer nucleosome function/DNA wrapping/oligomeric state to TAF, NC2, NF-Y, CHRAC, Sos or bacterial proteins. Linker histones correctly placed in a.4.5.13 with the caveat that absence of assertion is not proof of non-homology. Limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineages, sunids, superfamily comment, and the five sibling families all supported by bundle calls. Frames relationship as remote homology at superfamily level with separate families implying low sequence similarity; fold/class add nothing further. Rejects transfer of HisE reaction/pathway to SSo12199 and MazG activity to HisE, plus oligomeric, template, and phenotype inferences, noting the hypothetical/UNL caveats. External evidence listed. Complete.

Correct families c.55.1.1/c.55.1.3/c.55.1.4, superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55, class, sunids, 16 child families, duplication comment, and homology flags all supported by bundle. Infers probable common ancestry of the catalytic core with conserved two-lobe nucleotide cleft, and explicitly refuses transfer of substrate, mechanism, kinetics, regulation, cellular role, sequence similarity, and templates; fold-level neighbours not strengthened to 'unrelated'. Factual slip: states SCOPe treats the duplicated pair as one classified domain spanning both halves, whereas SCOPe 2.08 splits each chain into two c.55.1 domains. Noncentral. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Biological interpretation complete: divergent evolution from a common ancestor with functional divergence, superfamily as the homology-bearing level, explicit limits on function/metal/oligomer transfer, and external evidence named; transparently labels chemistries as outside SCOPe data. Factual: cites 'deterministic pairwise comparisons' returning 'same_superfamily' with no caveats, but no compare endpoint output is in the evidence bundle (only parents/annotations for d2za7a_, d1mxra_, d1o9ia_); the lowest-shared-node conclusion is derivable but the cited comparison output is unsupported. Other identifiers and annotations (mutant, automated match) supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, superfamily, fold comment, homology endpoint (including fold-level warning) and curator comments all match the bundle. Correctly distinguishes superfamily homology from fold similarity, refuses copper/ET transfer citing the lacking-metal-site annotations, lists required external evidence, and avoids over-reading SAG1 as non-homologous. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Verified lineage, sunids, Pfam xrefs, 11 families, homology flags, domain sids (d1ubqa_, d1wj4a1 8-118, d1i42a_, d1rfaa_) and the 'Structural genomics target' comment all supported. Superfamily presented as probable common origin with families as divergent roles; fold-level sharing explicitly not a homology claim nor a non-homology claim. Rejects transfer of conjugation, Ras binding (incl. to d.15.1.10), p97 binding, Pfam merging, interface templates, fold-level neighbours; notes automated-match provenance; required external evidence listed. Minor unverifiable SUMO-3 only.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All three families, sunids, representative domains (d3chya_, d1orda1 1ord A:1-107, d1r8ja2 1r8j A:2-135), KaiA C-terminal a.186.1.1 and d7odca1 b.49.2.3 are supported by the bundle. States superfamily as deepest homology-bearing node, declines to strengthen fold-level similarity to 'unrelated', rejects transfer of phosphoreceiver signaling, clock function, and PLP decarboxylation, correctly reads 'complexed with plp' as an entry-level ligand note, and notes ODC is multi-domain (recruitment). Minor: cites a 'deterministic pairwise comparison' endpoint not present in the bundle, though the stated result is derivable from the parent lineages.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All facts verified: b.84.5 (310577), b.84.5.1 (310616), protein entries 310706/310707, d3a5ca3 and d1vdza2 boundaries, five sibling superfamilies with sunids/comments, PubMed xref, 1.75 fold having only four superfamilies. Clearly frames superfamily as the ancestry-asserting level, fold as architecture only, and states the separate superfamily is not an assertion of analogy/convergence (operational SCOPe-negative, not proven non-homolog). Positive homology claim among bulge domains in b.84.5.1 stated. Rejects unsafe function and template transfers across b.84 superfamilies. Honest about limits of API rationale and release coverage.

Complete and accurate: all three superfamilies with sunids, families, and curator comments verified; homology endpoint used correctly; explicitly states separate superfamilies are not proof of analogy/convergence; flags 'possible link' as curator speculation not classification; lists needed independent evidence. Notes automated-match family and release scope.

Identifiers, 13-family composition, sole-superfamily status of fold c.2, fold and family comments, PF02254 and homology-endpoint results all match the bundle. Interpretation correctly puts the homology claim at the superfamily, describes divergence into oxidoreductase, CoA-binding and channel-gating roles, and notes the superfamily name 'NAD(P)-binding' is a historical descriptor rather than a guarantee of ligand. Explicit limits on function, ligand, template and cross-fold inferences, with a candid statement that historical placements were not verified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All must_include met: shared family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), explicit 'not a true family' comment cited as disclaiming the family-level inference, class k context, correct sunids and ligand comments. Notes the curator comment overrides the mechanical homology flag and that SCOPe makes no statement on design lineage; no-transfer limits given. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met with verified 1.69 and 2.08 lineages for both domains, level-by-level comparison (class shared both releases; fold and superfamily newly shared; families still distinct), compare result same_superfamily at 52309. Correctly explains that SCOPe moved from no homology assertion to probable common ancestry, that the SID change (d1t1ja_ -> d1t1ja1) is due to the class l tag split and not the evolutionary change, and that sunids should be used for cross-release tracking. Rejects function and template transfer. Minor: says the API does not expose the intermediate release, when it could have been queried; this is framed as a self-reported limit and does not introduce an error.

Complete and fully supported: full lineages with sunids for both domains, homology responses accurately quoted for both, explicit list of unsafe transfers (tag hit as Ig evidence, untrimmed chain as template, class-l co-membership as ancestry). No material errors.

Correct 1.75 single-domain record with full lineage and correct 2.08 pair with sunids, boundaries, and both new lineages, including the retirement of the old fold node. Makes the required inference that the recurring N-terminal unit is the evolutionary module while the chain recurs nowhere, uses the retrieved fold comment to note the C-terminal region is itself a candidate for further subdivision, and calibrates transfer to family versus superfamily versus fold. Explicitly does not identify the release in which the split first appeared, leaving the 2.04 comparison unmet.

All five domains correct; uses family annotations (PubMed 21441348/23354046, Pfam IDs, fold comment) that are supported by the bundle; verifies d.394 absent in 2.06 and present in 2.07. Mosaic interpretation with reused modules vs new fold, superfamily-vs-family distinctions, no function transfer, and explicit limits. No material errors.

Complete: identical lineage to family a.298.1.1 with sunids and species, the roughly 15-fold length span tabulated, the 're' heterogeneity code quoted as the curatorial statement that family membership rests on a shared small repeating unit in differing copy number, the 'single repeat' comment, and the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 correctly restricted to BurrH numbering. Repeat counts are flagged as interpretation rather than curated values, external knowledge is labeled as such, specificity and template transfer are refused, quality ranking is declined, and claims are release-scoped to 2.08. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Reports stable 2.08 (2.08-stable, freeze/release dates) and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16, all supported by the /releases/current evidence bundle. Recommends citing 2.08 pinned in release-scoped calls, warns against bare 'current', and says to record the full dated label plus stable base when periodic-only entries are used. Correctly describes periodic updates as incremental additions that do not rewrite the stable classification and are not a new stable release. States the endpoint's limits.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All facts bundle-supported (lineage, ms flags on all four fragment domains, fold homology warning, 1.75 sunid 17771 vs 2.08 302344 automated match, d3c98b_ as unflagged full domain). Reasoning covers fragment bias (fold inherited by family homology, three helices cannot satisfy four-helix fold), spectrin warning without homology or analogy claim, value of complete domain for templates, representative choice d3c98b_, function transfer limited to family-level ancestry. Limits stated. Quality values cited for selection only.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Directly answers: divergence within c.2.1 (including non-NAD members), convergence consistent with but not proven by separate folds, explicit limit that different placement is absence of a positive homology assertion, four clear reasons cofactor/active-site similarity is insufficient, and a complete list of evidence required. All sunids, curator comments, family lists and homology-endpoint values match the bundle; d.58 superfamily count claim is consistent with the (truncated) children listing.

States both release states precisely, including 2.04 folds b.23 versus b.18 with class-only sharing and 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 retained separately. Cites the curated PubMed 17977833 note and correctly identifies the Cry4Ba sibling in the Cry3A family as the link, quotes both fold strand-count descriptions, and treats structure-comparison results explicitly as representative-derived from 1nqjA with competing non-b.18 hits acknowledged, which is unusually careful reasoning about why fold similarity alone does not discriminate. Bars function and template transfer and lists what was not inspected, including the unread publication and residue-level correspondence. Numeric hit values are supported by the retrieved 1nqjA hits body in its bundle.

Bundle facts correct; homology at family/superfamily/protein level preserved, hf described as different 3D arrangement with a.4 inherited, rejects reciprocal template use, says exclude or stratify as hf example with caveat preserved, notes both are mutants, declines quality ranking since values not retrieved. One imprecision: states d1p7jd_ is 'in complex with DNA' based on the nhe comment; the entry has no DNA.

Verified facts (lineage, fr inconsistency scope/inherited, comment, 50-residue ATOM sequence vs 99 nominal and 104 for d1uc6a1, 1uc6 quality) match bundle; 1o5d quality values correct though not in bundle. Clearly separates structural-instance caveat from evolutionary placement, explains partial-coverage alignment and misleading scores, warns that quality scores would wrongly favour the fragment, recommends excluding or stratifying the fragment in a labelled stratum and choosing among complete candidates after quality retrieval, notes the fragment flag persists through identity filtering, and limits function transfer. Honest about unretrieved d1o5dt1 annotations and unknown cause of missing residues. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

All must_include met: new superfamily in existing fold, family = strong homology claim, new fold only for different core topology, placement as revisable evidence-integrating hypothesis; explicit that superfamily split is asymmetric and not proof of analogy/convergence; rejects fold-based function transfer; notes nf/hf and manual curation. Factual deduction: states release 2.08 details were 'confirmed from the API' but the evidence bundle is empty, so that API-dependent claim is unsupported (noncentral). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Complete correct facts (class/fold/superfamily/family sunids, comments, homology records with fold warning), all supported. Separates fold-level structural statement from superfamily-level homology claim, treats shared mechanism as hypothesis consistent with homology, flags HRD/DFG as literature not SCOPe. Explicitly lists non-transferable properties (substrate class, acceptor residue, regiospecificity, isoform preference, regulation, templates). Evidence list complete. No material errors.
